protocol.name: dashi_chrome_v1
protocol.description:
Dashi-private. By default dashi-comp draws a title bar above every window that accepts server-side decorations. This protocol lets an app put its own content in that strip: with the "unified" style there is no title bar, the window's surface runs up to the top edge, and the compositor draws only its traffic lights (close, minimize, zoom) over the surface at the top-left.
The app moves the window itself with xdg_toplevel.move from its empty toolbar areas, and zooms it from a double click with xdg_toplevel.set_maximized / unset_maximized. A press on a traffic light goes to the compositor, never to the surface.

interface.name: dashi_chrome_manager_v1
interface.description: A global that makes a dashi_chrome_v1 for an xdg_toplevel.

entry.name: chrome_exists
entry.summary: the toplevel already has a dashi_chrome_v1

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Chrome objects it made stay valid.

request.name: get_chrome

description.summary: get the chrome of a toplevel

request.description: Make the chrome object of `toplevel`. A toplevel has at most one; a second request is a chrome_exists protocol error until the first is destroyed.

interface.name: dashi_chrome_v1
interface.description:
Sets how the compositor frames one toplevel. Destroying the object puts the toplevel back to the standard style.
The style is read when the window first has a size and follows later changes, but set it before the first commit to avoid a visible shift: the compositor places the surface where the unified or standard layout puts it.

entry.name: standard
entry.summary: the compositor's title bar above the surface

entry.name: unified
entry.summary: no title bar; traffic lights over the surface

request.name: set_style
request.description: The compositor honors "unified" only for windows it would decorate itself: the toplevel has no xdg_toplevel_decoration, or its mode is server_side. An app that asked for client_side draws all of it. When the style is not honored, the controls event reports an empty rectangle.

event.name: controls

description.summary: the area of the traffic lights

event.description:
The rectangle, in surface-local logical coordinates, that the traffic lights occupy including their margins. Leave it empty (no buttons, no text) and start toolbar content past it; the compositor draws over it and takes presses in it.
Sent when the style takes effect or stops, and again when the rectangle changes (for example with the output's scale). A rectangle with zero width and height means there are no controls: the style is standard, or unified was not honored.
